findings.title: Burden bullet 'no probe → implementation or unclear' contradicts the design-or-model row and blocks architectural codes at deterministic boundaries
findings.section: Step 3 class table, 'Design or model, not separated' (line 317); Class rules, Burden (lines 322-323); Step 2b (iii) (line 248)
findings.problem:
Line 323 is an unconditional bullet: 'Where the case has no probe, the code is implementation defect or unclear.' Draft 4's new row (line 317) makes design-or-model available for 'routing, reading, A2's support check, or any case if Step 2b is not run'. These cannot both hold:
(1) If Step 2b is not run, no case has a probe. Line 323 then forces implementation defect or unclear, so the row's 'any case if Step 2b is not run' can never apply.
(2) Probe (iii) runs only where the offline check shows the holding key was pruned out. A reading case whose holding key was in the question-time prompt has no probe. Line 322 says a probe-type alternative is ruled out 'only by its probe returning not recovered', so this case is forced to implementation defect or unclear, although the offline check already refutes the shortlist cause. The 'reading' branch of the row is unreachable for exactly the cases where implementation has been excluded.
(3) Read literally, line 323 also covers every deterministic boundary with no probe at all, such as A0/A1 state rules. Architectural weakness and trade-off then become impossible there, which contradicts the class table and the WD-cases rule.
findings.proposed_change:
Line 323: 'Where a probe-type alternative applies at the case's caused-at boundary and has no probe output (Step 2b not run, case not probed, or no output), the code is implementation defect or unclear.'
Line 322: append 'or by the offline check showing that the item the alternative would restore was present in the recorded prompt (resolver or question-time).'
Line 317: replace 'or any case if Step 2b is not run' with 'and, where Step 2b is not run, only boundaries with no probe-type alternative (e.g. A2's support check)'.

findings.title: Probes (ii-r)/(ii-h): mixed-path cases cannot pass either probe, and their 'not recovered' then rules out both alternatives; re-extracted claims have no matching rule
findings.problem:
Each probe keeps the other path's claims on their recorded keys ('unprobed claims kept on their recorded keys'). Take a routing-lost case whose misfiled claims lie on both paths, for example a hint-misfiled carrier and a resolver-misfiled rival:
- (ii-r) fails in every repeat, because the hint-routed claim stays misfiled;
- (ii-h) fails in every repeat, because the resolver-routed claim stays misfiled.
k = k0 = 0 in both, so both read 'not recovered'. Line 266 then counts this as evidence against an implementation cause, and line 322 counts both probe-type alternatives (unpruned resolution and re-hinting) as ruled out. The coder may then reach design-or-model or architectural on a result that could never have recovered. The text also does not settle whether 'every probed claim of the case' pools (ii-r) and (ii-h) claims. If it does, a joint recovery cannot be mapped, because the mapping assigns (ii-r) and (ii-h) to different boundaries.
Separately, (ii-h) re-extracts a span, which yields new claims. Nothing says how the probed carrier or rival is identified in that output, or whether a repeat passes when the carrier, or the rival, is absent from it.
findings.proposed_change:
Add to Scoring:
- 'A case whose misfiled claims lie on both paths forms output j from (ii-r) repeat j together with (ii-h) (b) repeat j. Its control output j is the recorded-resolver repeat j with the (a) repeat j. A recovery maps to routing, path unclear (possible implementation at both). Its not-recovered result rules out both alternatives. A single-path probe's not-recovered rules out only that path's alternative, and only for cases whose misfiled claims all lie on that path.'
- 'In (ii-h), the probed claim is the re-extracted claim that the loss-trace matcher matches to it, adjudicated where the matcher is unsure. A carrier with no match fails the repeat. A rival with no match passes.'

findings.title: The A2 leave-one-out sets caused-at but is not a pending output, so A2 codes cannot be conditional on it and its moves count as 'discretionary'
findings.section: Class rules, Pending results (lines 325-328); Caused-at, A2 cases (line 359); Order of work item 8 (lines 396-400); Frozen inputs v1/v2 rule (line 86)
findings.problem:
Line 359 lets an A2 contract's leave-one-out set an A2 case's caused-at. The leave-one-out is a Step 2 output, sealed until item 7. Line 325 lists the sealed outputs that make an alternative pending: a 2b probe, the offline reading check, an oracle row result and the WD result. The leave-one-out is not among them, although con3 item 5 and con5 item 3 both named it. Three consequences:
- Pass-1 and V4 codes for A2 cases, which are half of the 180 sampled cases, cannot be conditional on it.
- Item 8's re-coding covers only 'where the oracle moves a case's boundary'.
- Item 8 logs a change as mechanical only if it is 'from the pending results'. Boundary moves by the leave-one-out, the class and sub-cause re-codes at any moved boundary, and the re-codes line 86 requires where v1 and v2 differ are therefore logged as discretionary. That inflates the anchoring measure, which con5 asked to keep free of forced changes.
findings.proposed_change:
- Line 325: add 'an A2 leave-one-out result' to the sealed outputs.
- Line 326: 'recovered: the probe mapping, the oracle rule, the leave-one-out rule (line 359) or the WD rule sets the code'.
- Item 8: 'Where the oracle or a leave-one-out moves a case's boundary…'.
- Line 398: 'mechanical (from the pending results, including re-codes at a boundary they move and the v1/v2 re-codes of line 86, logged by kind)'.

findings.title: (ii-r) mapping fixes one sub-cause and mislabels expansion-routed claims
findings.problem:
con4 item 3 is not adopted. Every (ii-r) recovery maps to 'shortlist or prune excluded a fitting key', even when the offline (ii) check shows the fitting key was in the recorded resolver prompt.
For expansion-routed claims the probe tests the wrong step. In the code (`state_key_resolution_service.py` resolve_state_key_for_claim), the resolver first returns no key, and the expansion service then reuses or creates the key. The recorded-prompt control returns no key, which 'also passes' when no registered key fits. So k0 ≥ 2, and the case reads 'not reproduced (sampling instability)', although the misfiling came from the reuse threshold or the harness reviewer.
findings.proposed_change:
- Restrict (ii-r) to resolver-routed claims. Code expansion-routed misfilings from the trace under criterion (iii) (reuse or similarity threshold) or the harness-reviewer entry.
- Mapping: 'shortlist or prune excluded a fitting key' only where the offline check shows the fitting key was missing from the recorded prompt. Otherwise the sub-cause is set on the page within key resolution.

findings.title: C/C2 differ between harness and live checks; the V4 fallback and a late audit are ambiguous
findings.section: Step 4 configurations and checks (lines 462-480, 493); V4 fallback (lines 412-416); Frozen inputs (line 86)
findings.problem:
- **Harness configurations.** The harness replays recorded LLM outputs, so harness C and C2 can include only repairs whose effect is deterministic. An accepted (a) repair upstream of an LLM call is silently absent.
- **Shared C set.** One live C set is shared 'in that period'. A state-logic or (a) repair admitted after the set ran makes it differ from C.
- **Live A2-only repairs.** For an A2-only routing or extraction repair checked live, 'the contract's leave-one-out … computed with the repair on' cannot run in the A2 harness, which replays only the recorded A2 runs.
- **V4 fallback.** 'Only (a) conformance repairs proceed' leaves it unclear whether WD and A2-contract admission are suspended.
- **Late audit.** If the blind codes arrive but the audit does not, v2 is undefined, although 'the oracles are always computed under both'.
findings.proposed_change:
- 'In the harness, C and C2 contain only repairs that need no LLM call; any others are listed.'
- 'Every (a) and state-logic repair is settled before the shared C set runs; a later change to C re-runs it.'
- 'A live A2′ repair's contract leave-one-out runs on A2′ runs that pass the A2 gate; otherwise the repair is not checkable.'
- State whether WD and the contracts are admitted under the fallback.
- 'If the audit is late, v2 = v1 and this is reported.'

result.reasoning:
The finding is correct, and nothing else in draft 4 deals with it. Checked against the draft:

- **The leave-one-out is sealed.** It is a Step 2 output ("A2, offline", line 214), and item 7 (line 394) keeps every Step 2 output closed until the reveal.
- **It sets caused-at.** Line 359 lets it set caused-at for A2 cases. There are 90 of them: 30 per run over a2_r1, a2_r2b and a2_r3, which is half the 180.
- **It is not a pending output.** Line 325 lists only a 2b probe, the offline reading check, an oracle row result and the WD result. Line 326 names only the probe, oracle and WD rules. A blind coder therefore cannot make an A2 code conditional on it.
- **Item 8 does not cover it.** Line 397 re-codes only where "the oracle" moves a boundary. The oracles are defined as R, R-hint/resolver, E+R and E+R* (lines 192-197), and the leave-one-out is not among them. Line 398 counts a change as mechanical only if it comes "from the pending results". So a caused-at moved by the leave-one-out, and the re-code that follows, would be logged as discretionary.
- **The line-86 re-codes are not covered either.** Line 86 requires re-coding where v1 and v2 differ. Item 8 does not say who makes these re-codes or how they are logged.
- **The draft lost the earlier fix.** con3 item 5 and con5 item 3 both asked for the leave-one-out to count as a forced or mechanical change. Draft 4 kept the pending-results structure but dropped that.

**Two corrections to the proposed change:**

1. **The fallback.** If the leave-one-out simply joins line 325's list, line 328's fallback applies to it ("no output: implementation defect or unclear"). An A2 run that fails the A2 gate produces no leave-one-out. Every case on that run, 30 per run, would then become implementation-or-unclear. That contradicts line 359's "Otherwise caused-at comes from the page". The leave-one-out only sets caused-at, so with no output it should fall back to the page. The oracle has the same problem: on a gate-failing A0/A1 run, line 328 conflicts with the Default rule at line 361.
2. **The label.** Re-codes of class and sub-cause at a moved boundary, and the v1/v2 re-codes, are made by a coder after the reveal. They are forced, but they are not mechanical. Calling them "mechanical" would hide judgement that may be anchored on the revealed results. They should be a separate logged category, left out of the anchoring measure and reported with their own between-coder agreement. This is the "forced, by kind" split that con5 asked for.

The finding holds against draft 4 (thesis/notes/thesis_completion/artifacts/23-plan-amendment-1-ceilings-and-root-cause.md). The review3 files were not at the stated scratchpad path, so this check rests on the draft text alone.

1) Mixed-path cases fail by construction. Line 246 keeps unprobed claims on their recorded keys. A case output passes only if no claim of another matter shares a key with a carrier.
- Take a hint-misfiled carrier with a resolver-misfiled rival. Under (ii-r), the carrier stays on a key held by another matter. Under (ii-h), the rival stays on the carrier's key. Both probes therefore score k=0 in every repeat. The control also fails, so k0=0 and "not reproduced" (line 254) does not catch it.
- Mixed cases are plausible. Line 45 says 69 of 203 routing-lost rows had at least one carrier keyed by a path other than the hint, and the paths of rivals are not reported.

2) That spurious 'not recovered' feeds two rules:
- Line 266: "evidence against an implementation cause at that boundary".
- Line 322: a probe-type alternative is ruled out only by "not recovered". Both unpruned resolution and re-hinting would count as ruled out.
- It also meets line 317's design-or-model condition, "every available in-design probe was not recovered".

The only protection is line 358's "routing, path unclear", and it is not reliable:
- Line 358 assumes a single misrouted claim. Line 361's tie rule covers boundaries that would each have prevented the loss, not two that are both needed.
- A coder could read the carrier as "the misrouted claim" and assign a single path. Even if path unclear is applied, the rule set still contradicts itself: the caused-at says possible implementation at both, while the probe rules out both alternatives.

3) Pooling is mostly settled by line 252: k is "for a case and a condition", so (ii-r) and (ii-h) are separate. That separation is what produces the defect above, so the ambiguity point is minor.

4) Identification in (ii-h) is only half covered:
- Line 228 says probes are scored with the loss-trace matcher, which can find carriers of the gold value in re-extracted output.
- It does not say how a rival is found in that output (the matcher matches against gold values, not other matters), what happens when several claims match, or what happens when the carrier or the rival is missing.

The proposed change goes in the right direction but has one flaw. A joint not-recovered should not rule out a path whose own claims passed. For example, the unpruned resolver may fix the rival in every repeat while the hint path still fails. That resolver-path alternative worked, and ruling it out would push the case toward non-implementation codes, against the plan's burden rule. The matcher wording also needs a separate rule for rivals.
result.better_change:
Add to Step 2b (ii) Scoring, after line 247:
- "A misfiled claim is a carrier or rival whose matter does not fit its recorded key's definition (as at line 358). A case whose misfiled claims all lie on one path takes only that path's probe. The other path's probe is not applicable to it, and its result is reported but never counts as 'not recovered'. A case with misfiled claims on both paths takes a joint condition. Output j combines (ii-r) repeat j with (ii-h) (b) repeat j. The control output j combines the recorded-resolver repeat j with (ii-h) (a) repeat j. Each probed claim's own pass/fail is recorded per repeat."
- "In (ii-h), a carrier's re-extracted counterparts are the output claims that the loss-trace matcher matches to the gold value, adjudicated where the matcher is unsure. A rival's counterparts are the output claims that the adjudicators judge to state the recorded rival's matter. Every counterpart must pass. A carrier with no counterpart fails the repeat. A rival with no counterpart passes the repeat, and the case is listed as recovered-by-omission (sub-cause extraction, not hinting)."

In Mapping (lines 261-266), add:
- "Joint condition recovered: routing, path unclear (possible implementation at both)."
- "Joint condition not recovered: rules out a path's alternative only if that path's own probed claims failed in every repeat. A path whose claims passed in at least 2 of 3 repeats is left as possible implementation at that path."
- "A single-path probe's 'not recovered' rules out only that path's alternative, and only for cases whose misfiled claims all lie on that path."

In Burden (line 322), after "returning not recovered", add ", where that probe is applicable to the case under Step 2b (ii)".

In Caused-at (line 358), add: "A case with misfiled claims on both paths is coded routing, path unclear, unless the joint probe rule above rules out one path."
